result:
Four circles give C(4,2) = 6 pairs, and each pair meets in at most 2 points, so there are at most 12 intersection points. Twelve is achievable: four circles in general position, each pair crossing at two distinct points with no three circles sharing a point, give exactly 12 distinct points.

Solution A uses exactly this reasoning and reaches 12.

Solution B reaches 14, which exceeds the upper bound of 12. Its counting is also inconsistent. It has all circles pass through A and B, which makes those shared points, and then adds new points beyond what the pairs allow.

WINNER: A
